stemBlocks.value: (a) Vector PQ = (5, −4) (column vector). If P is the point (−2, 3), determine the coordinates of Q. (b) In pentagon OABCD, OA is parallel to DC and AB is parallel to OD, with OD = 2AB and OA = 2DC. Given OA = a and AB = b, find in terms of a and b, in simplest form: (vi) AD, (vii) BC, and (viii) state the conclusion about AD and BC that follows.
Think first: A column vector tells you how far to move, so Q is P shifted by (5, −4); the pentagon then needs OD and DC written in terms of a and b before any route is built.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p280-q03 from workbook page 280.

solutionSteps.instruction: Add the components of PQ to the coordinates of P.
Translate the two given conditions into vectors. AB is parallel to OD with OD = 2AB, and OA is parallel to DC with OA = 2DC.
Travel from A to D through O.
Travel from B to C through A, O and D.

contentBlocks.value: BC = BA + AO + OD + DC = −b − a + 2b + (1/2)a
Result: AD and BC are parallel, with AD twice the length of BC

strategyBlocks.value: Add the column vector to the coordinates of P for part (a). For (b), turn the parallel/length statements into OD = 2b and DC = (1/2)a, then build AD and BC as chains of known vectors and compare them.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) Q = (3, −1)  (b) (vi) AD = 2b − a  (vii) BC = b − (1/2)a = (1/2)(2b − a)  (viii) BC = (1/2)AD, so AD and BC are parallel and AD is twice as long as BC.

whyThisWorks.value: A column vector is a pure displacement: adding it to a point's coordinates moves that point without changing anything else, which is why Q = P + PQ. In the pentagon, 'parallel' means one vector is a scalar multiple of the other, and the length statements fix the scalar, so OD and DC can be written entirely in a and b. Once both AD and BC are expressed in the same two vectors, one being a multiple of the other proves the parallel relationship and the length ratio in a single line.

commonErrors.misconception: Subtracting the column vector from P instead of adding it, giving (−7, 7).

commonErrors.misconception: Setting DC = 2a instead of (1/2)a — read carefully which is twice which.

examTip.value: Convert every worded condition ('X is parallel to Y and twice as long') into an equation in vectors before you start any route — the algebra then does itself.
